types.embedding_query_text: Country: A sovereign state or nation. Also called nation, state. Examples: UK, Greenland, Iceland, Spain.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: All mentions are countries, matching the Country class.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: UKNonprofitType
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific non-profit organization types recognized within the United Kingdom. Also called UK charity type, British non-profit category, UK voluntary sector classification. Examples: a registered charity, a community interest company (CIC), a benevolent society.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: Continent: A large continuous landmass. Also called landmass. Examples: Europe.

chosen_type.label: Continent
chosen_type.justification: Europe is a continent, matching the Continent class.

candidates.label: Continent
candidates.comment: One of the Earth's large landmasses, such as Europe or Africa. Also called major landmass, global region, land continent. Examples: Asia, North America, Antarctica, Australia. Distinct from Landform, which is a general term for a natural feature of the Earth's surface.

candidates.label: Mountain
candidates.comment: A landform that is a large natural elevation of the earth's surface, typically rising to a summit. Also called peak, mount, range. Examples: "Mount Everest", "Mount Fuji", "Rocky Mountains", "Mount Kilimanjaro". Distinct from Landform, which is a broader category for natural geographical features.

candidates.label: Landform
candidates.comment: A Landform is a place representing a natural physical feature of the Earth's surface. Also called geographical feature, terrain feature, natural formation. Examples: mountain, plain, valley, island, river. Distinct from Place, which is a broader category for any location.

candidates.label: BodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A Landform representing a significant accumulation of water, such as a sea, ocean, or lake. Also called aquatic environment, water body, large water mass. Examples: "The Pacific Ocean", "Lake Superior", "The Mediterranean Sea", "The Nile River". Distinct from Beach, which is a specific landform adjacent to a body of water.

candidates.label: Volcano
candidates.comment: A landform, typically a mountain, with a vent through which lava, rock fragments, hot vapor, and gas are ejected. Also called active volcano, dormant volcano, volcanic mountain. Examples: Mount Fuji, Mount Vesuvius, Kilauea.

types.embedding_query_text: AstronomicalEvent: A natural phenomenon occurring in space or involving celestial bodies. Also called celestial event, cosmic event. Examples: solar eclipse, eclipse.

chosen_type.label: AstronomicalEvent
chosen_type.definition: A natural phenomenon occurring in space or involving celestial bodies.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org event type covers astronomical phenomena like solar eclipses.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent
candidates.comment: An event focused on literature, such as readings, book launches, or discussions. Also called book event, author appearance, literary gathering. Examples: a poetry reading, a book signing, a literary festival, a panel discussion with authors.

candidates.label: BroadcastEvent
candidates.comment: A BroadcastEvent is a PublicationEvent representing an event that is transmitted over the air or online. Also called live broadcast, streamed event, televised event, radio broadcast. Examples: a live news report, a sports game broadcast, a concert livestream.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

types.embedding_query_text: CelestialBody: A natural object in space, such as a star, planet, or moon. Also called astronomical object, heavenly body. Examples: Moon, Sun.

chosen_type.label: CelestialBody
chosen_type.definition: A natural object in space, such as a moon, planet, or star.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class matches celestial bodies; mentions are Moon and Sun.

candidates.label: RiverBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A natural flowing watercourse, typically freshwater, flowing towards an ocean, sea, lake, or another river. Also called river, stream, waterway, current. Examples: the Nile River, the Amazon River, the Mississippi River, the Thames. Distinct from SeaBodyOfWater, which is a large expanse of saltwater.

candidates.label: OceanBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: An OceanBodyOfWater, as a BodyOfWater, is a large expanse of saltwater, such as the Pacific Ocean. Also called ocean, sea, marine body. Examples: Atlantic Ocean, Indian Ocean, Southern Ocean. Distinct from LakeBodyOfWater, which is an inland freshwater body.

candidates.label: LakeBodyOfWater
candidates.comment: A LakeBodyOfWater is a landform representing a large body of still water surrounded by land. Also called lake, inland sea, reservoir. Examples: Lake Superior, Lake Tahoe, Lake Pontchartrain. Distinct from River, which is flowing water, and OceanBodyOfWater, which is a large saltwater body.

candidates.label: Person

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct

Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: WarrantyScope
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing the range of services covered by a warranty in case of product defect or malfunction. Also called warranty coverage, guarantee scope, service level. Examples: "Parts and Labor - Bring In", "Labor - On Site", "Parts Only".

candidates.label: OfficeEquipmentStore
candidates.comment: An OfficeEquipmentStore is a local business that sells supplies and equipment for offices. Also called office supply store, stationery shop, business equipment retailer. Examples: Staples, Office Depot, a local stationery shop. Distinct from ComputerStore, which specializes in computers.

candidates.label: Optician
candidates.comment: An Optician is a local business that sells reading glasses and similar devices for improving vision. Also called optical store, eyewear shop, optometrist's office (if selling glasses). Examples: LensCrafters, a local independent optician, an online glasses retailer. Distinct from Ophthalmologist, who is a medical doctor specializing in eye care.

candidates.label: HealthPlanNetwork
candidates.comment: A HealthPlanNetwork is an intangible collection of healthcare providers, such as doctors and hospitals, that contract with a health insurance plan to provide services at negotiated rates. Also called provider network, insurance network, healthcare provider group. Examples: an HMO network, a PPO network, a specific hospital system affiliated with an insurer.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

types.embedding_query_text: Business: A commercial establishment. Also called shop, enterprise. Examples: bakery.

chosen_type.label: Bakery
chosen_type.justification: Mention 'bakery' is a specific type of business, matching Bakery.

candidates.label: Bakery

candidates.label: Store
candidates.comment: A retail business that sells goods to consumers. Also called shop, retail outlet, boutique, market. Examples: a grocery store, a clothing store, an electronics store, a bookstore.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: OnlineBusiness
candidates.comment: An OnlineBusiness is a particular business that operates primarily or entirely online. Also called e-business, internet business, digital enterprise. Examples: an e-commerce site, an online travel agency, a virtual doctor's office. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which has a physical presence.

candidates.label: MedicalBusiness
candidates.comment: A local business operating for medical purposes, which can be physical or virtual. Also called healthcare business, medical practice, health services provider. Examples: a dental office, a physical therapy clinic, a telemedicine service, a diagnostic lab. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which is a broader category for any local business.

candidates.label: HowToItem
candidates.comment: A HowToItem is a list item used as either a tool or supply when following instructions in a HowTo guide. Also called instruction component, how-to resource, procedural element. Examples: a screwdriver, flour, a measuring cup, a specific software application.

candidates.label: MediaReviewItem

candidates.label: Residence

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Duration

types.embedding_query_text: Ratio: A quantitative relationship between two amounts. Also called proportion, factor. Examples: 400 times.

chosen_type.label: Ratio
chosen_type.definition: A quantitative relationship between two amounts.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class matches a ratio like '400 times'.

candidates.label: QuantitativeValue
candidates.comment: A QuantitativeValue is a StructuredValue representing a point value or interval for product characteristics or other purposes. Also called numerical value, measurable value. Examples: a product's weight of '5 kg', a temperature range of '20-25°C', a height of '1.8 meters', a price of '$99.99'. Distinct from QualitativeValue, which represents a predefined, non-numeric value.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: InteractionCounter
candidates.comment: An InteractionCounter is a structured value summarizing how users have interacted with a CreativeWork. Also called engagement metric, user interaction count, activity tracker. Examples: number of likes, view count, comment count, share count.

candidates.label: Distance
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Distance represents a numerical value combined with a unit of length. Also called length, extent, span, separation. Examples: "10 km", "5 miles", "300 meters", "2 feet".

types.embedding_query_text: TimeDuration: The length of time something lasts. Also called period, span. Examples: 18 months, 400 years, less than two minutes.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are time durations, matching the Duration class.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Percentage: A fraction expressed as a part of 100. Also called proportion, percent. Examples: 90%, 95%, 45%, 99%.

chosen_type.label: Percentage
chosen_type.definition: A number expressed as a fraction of 100, such as 70%.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class matches percentages like 90%.

candidates.label: Integer
candidates.comment: Integer is a data type representing a whole number without a fractional component. Also called whole number, natural number (if positive), counting number. Examples: 0, 1, -5, 1000. Distinct from Float, which includes decimal values.

candidates.label: HyperTocEntry
candidates.comment: A HyperTocEntry is a creative work representing an individual item or section within a HyperToc, specifying its associated media and time offsets. Also called table of contents item, media chapter, section marker. Examples: 'Introduction (0:00-5:30)', 'Keynote Speech (10:15-30:00)', 'Q&A Session (30:00-45:00)'.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

candidates.label: Float
candidates.comment: Float is a Number data type representing a floating-point number. Also called decimal number, real number. Examples: 3.14, -0.5, 100.0, 2.718.

types.embedding_query_text: AstronomicalObject Examples: Universe.

chosen_type.label: AstronomicalObject
chosen_type.definition: A natural object or phenomenon existing in outer space.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class matches astronomical objects like the Universe.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: AlignmentObject
candidates.comment: An AlignmentObject is an Intangible item describing a relationship or correspondence between a learning resource and a node in an educational framework. Also called learning alignment, competency mapping, educational standard link. Examples: A resource aligned to a specific Common Core State Standard, a course module mapped to a learning outcome, a textbook chapter linked to a curriculum objective.

candidates.label: MediaObject
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a media object like an image, video, audio, or text, which can be embedded or downloaded. Also called digital media asset, multimedia file, content object. Examples: a JPEG image file, an MP4 video, an MP3 audio track, a PDF document. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: AudioObject
candidates.comment: An AudioObject is a MediaObject representing an audio file or recording. Also called audio file, sound recording, sound clip, audio track. Examples: an MP3 song, a podcast episode, a voice memo, a sound effect. Distinct from VideoObject, which contains visual content.

candidates.label: VideoObject
candidates.comment: A media object representing a video file. Also called video file, digital video, movie clip. Examples: an MP4 video, a YouTube video, a short film.
